pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these plants lives for many years? (1 mark)
   A. Mango tree
   B. Sukuma wiki grown for one season
   C. Beans
   D. Maize

2. A student says a tree is not alive because it does not move from place to place. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Trees are made of stone
   B. Plants show life by growing and responding
   C. Trees are not plants
   D. Only animals grow

3. Which part of a bean plant grows in the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves
   B. Roots
   C. Flowers
   D. Pods

4. How do most flowering plants make new plants? (1 mark)
   A. By giving birth
   B. By seeds
   C. By laying eggs
   D. By walking away

5. A student puts a plant in a box with a small hole on one side. After a week, the plant bends toward the hole. This shows that plants (1 mark)
   A. respond to light
   B. make sound
   C. need no water
   D. walk

6. What does a snail do when you touch it? (1 mark)
   A. Flies away
   B. Grows a tail
   C. Pulls its body into its shell
   D. Starts to sing

7. What is the waste passed out by animals called? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Urine and faeces
   C. Milk
   D. Seeds

8. What do fish use to take oxygen from water? (1 mark)
   A. Lungs
   B. Horns
   C. Gills
   D. Feathers

9. Which group of vertebrates has feathers? (1 mark)
   A. Amphibians
   B. Reptiles
   C. Fish
   D. Birds

10. Which of these animals gives birth to live young? (1 mark)
   A. Housefly
   B. Goat
   C. Hen
   D. Frog

11. A pupil finds a small animal under a stone. It has a long soft body, no legs and no shell. It is probably (1 mark)
   A. A lizard
   B. A frog
   C. An earthworm
   D. A snake

12. Which of these animals has an outside skeleton or hard covering and no backbone? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Tilapia
   C. Hen
   D. Crab

13. How often should teeth be brushed? (1 mark)
   A. Once a month
   B. At least twice a day
   C. Once a year
   D. Never

14. What are the symptoms of worms mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Loud voice
   B. Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   C. Fast running
   D. Clear skin

15. What does the small intestine mainly absorb? (1 mark)
   A. Air
   B. Digested food
   C. Sound
   D. Light

16. Another name for the gullet is (1 mark)
   A. Tongue
   B. Oesophagus
   C. Rectum
   D. Anus

17. What does the rectum do? (1 mark)
   A. Stores faeces for a short time
   B. Chews food
   C. Makes saliva
   D. Digests proteins

18. What is bloating? (1 mark)
   A. A cut in the mouth
   B. Tiredness
   C. Loose faeces
   D. A full, swollen tummy often with gas

19. What is the solid waste passed out through the anus called? (1 mark)
   A. Blood
   B. Faeces
   C. Juice
   D. Saliva

20. Why is it important to eat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. It stops you growing
   B. It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   C. It makes food taste of salt
   D. It makes you thirsty

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how a pupil can show that plants respond to light. (4 marks)

22. State any four signs of life in animals. (2 marks)

23. State three things a child should do when he has diarrhoea. (3 marks)

24. List four signs of life in plants. (2 marks)

25. Explain why we should care for animals and describe how it can be done at home and at school. (5 marks)

26. Describe how a pupil can tell that an earthworm is an animal. (3 marks)

27. Describe the differences between mammals and birds. (4 marks)

28. A pupil grows two bean seedlings. One is put in a cupboard and the other in the sunlight. Both are watered. After a week the two look different. Describe what she might see and give a reason. (4 marks)

29. A bat has wings. Explain why it is not a bird. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Mango tree
   Mango trees live for many years, while beans and maize live for one season.

2. B — Plants show life by growing and responding
   Plants show many signs of life even though they do not walk.

3. B — Roots
   Roots grow underground.

4. B — By seeds
   Most flowering plants reproduce by making seeds inside fruits.

5. A — respond to light
   The plant responds to the light entering through the hole.

6. C — Pulls its body into its shell
   This is a response to touch.

7. B — Urine and faeces
   Animals remove waste such as urine and faeces.

8. C — Gills
   Fish breathe using gills.

9. D — Birds
   Only birds have feathers.

10. B — Goat
   Goats are mammals and give birth to live young. Hens, frogs and flies lay eggs.

11. C — An earthworm
   An earthworm is a soft, legless invertebrate.

12. D — Crab
   A crab has a hard outer shell and no backbone.

13. B — At least twice a day
   Brushing morning and night keeps teeth healthy.

14. B — Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   These are signs that worms may be present.

15. B — Digested food
   Digested food passes through its wall into blood.

16. B — Oesophagus
   The gullet is also called the oesophagus.

17. A — Stores faeces for a short time
   The rectum stores faeces before they pass out.

18. D — A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   Bloating means the tummy feels full and swollen.

19. B — Faeces
   Faeces are the solid waste of the body.

20. B — It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   Chewing well breaks food down before swallowing.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put a plant in a box with a hole on one side. After some days the plant bends towards the hole showing it responds to light.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the set up, 1 mark for the hole giving light from one side, 1 mark for the plant bending, 1 mark for conclusion.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Feeding, growing, breathing, reproducing, removing waste, moving, responding to changes, dying (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tell an adult, drink clean water or ORS, and see a health worker. Keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any four of: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes, die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four correct signs.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals give us milk, meat, eggs and honey and help us in work. They are part of nature. We give them food, water, shelter and medical care and we do not hurt them. At school we keep the compound safe for birds.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for ways.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds on soil, grows, breathes, moves, responds to touch, reproduces and removes waste. It shows the signs of life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign, up to 3.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their young on milk and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and wings and lay eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four differences.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant in the cupboard looks weak and pale and the one in the light is green and healthy. Plants need light to make food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for describing each plant and 2 marks for the reason.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bat has fur and feeds its young on milk. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. So a bat is a mammal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fur, 1 mark for milk, 1 mark for mammal.
